messages.body_plain:
Masaki

I couple of ideas to test,
- if you loaded blavaan ahead of the model, dont use :: to call the bcfa function ( blavaan::bcfa ), just use bcfa
- You have very strict priors on the factor loadings, basically you are saying that all the factor loadings are ver close to 0
- Try running the example from the help page for the bcfa function ?bcfa, this is a simple model that we know it works. If this fails might be an issue with the installation of blavaan. But is this model works, and yours is not working, might be an issue with you data or model. Would help use narrow down were the problem might be

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit)

messages.subject: Re: Blavaan does not run Stan on macOS Catalina while Rstan and brms works fine.
messages.subject_clean: Blavaan does not run Stan on macOS Catalina while Rstan and brms works fine.
messages.body_plain:
Masaki,

My first guess is a versioning issue: your R version is somewhat old (pre 4.0), and it looks like you are using a development version of rstan (I believe that 2.21.2 is the newest version on CRAN). I personally haven't tested blavaan on the versions that you are using. If you installed rstan 2.21.3 after you installed blavaan, you might have to re-install blavaan so that it gets compiled with rstan 2.21.3.

Or, if you can, I might try the most up-to-date version of R paired with package versions on CRAN. But I realize you might have other reasons for using the versions you are using.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I know that I can use ppmc() and custom discrepancy functions for a range of procedures, but I am not sure if I can use to my advantage to achieve the following.

I am trying to do graphical ppmc as shown here: https://mc-stan.org/bayesplot/articles/graphical-ppcs.html and also analyse "prior predictives"  (graphically and using discrepancy function/residual analysis), as outlined in Schoot, R. van, Veen, D., Smeets, L., Winter, S. D., & Depaoli, S. (2020). A tutorial on using the WAMBS checklist to avoid the  misuse of Bayesian statistics. In R. van de Schoot & M. Miočevic (Eds.), Small Sample Size Solutions (pp. 30–49). Routledge.

One thing I would need is to generate simulated data using mcmc draws from a fitted model (rather than just the outcome of discrepancy functions) and based on random draws from just the model syntax (I guess I could do that using simulateData() from the lavaan package).

Is there some built-in method or an easy way to do this that I am missing?

Thanks for your help!
Robin

messages.body_plain:
Robin

We called it discrepancy function, beause that is the original use for model evluation with residuals, fit indices etc.

But the ppmc function has general use that can applied any function that you can applied with a "normal" lavaan object, across all posterior draws.

So, for what I understand you want (data sets predicted by each posterior draws), you can use the lavPredict(fit, type="ov") lavaan function as your discFUN. This function with the "ov" argument will gives you the predicted indicator scores based on the model

Hope this helps

messages.subject: blavaan syntax with equality constraints
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am encountering some issues with translating a working lavaan model into blavaan. My starting point is a MGCFA configural invariance model with effects coding (simple example with two groups):

model1 <-
'FAC =~
c(L11,L12)*var1 +
c(L21,L22)*var2 +
c(L31,L32)*var3 +
c(L41,L42)*var4 +
c(L51,L52)*var5

L51 == 5-L11-L21-L31-L41
L52 == 5-L12-L22-L32-L42

var1 ~ c(I11, I12)*1
var2 ~ c(I21, I22)*1
var3 ~ c(I31, I32)*1
var4 ~ c(I41, I42)*1
var5 ~ c(I51, I52)*1

0 == I11+I21+I31+I41+I51
0 == I12+I22+I32+I42+I52'

Running the following gives the desired output, where the loadings average to 1 and the intercepts sum to 0:

model.lavaan <- lavaan(model1,
                       data = dat,
                       group = "g",
                       estimator = "MLM",
                       int.ov.free = TRUE,
                       int.lv.free = TRUE,
                       auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                       auto.var = TRUE,
                       auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE)

If I apply the exact same model specification using blavaan:

model.blavaan1 <- blavaan(model1,
                          data = dat,
                          int.ov.free = TRUE,
                          int.lv.free = TRUE,
                          auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                          auto.var = TRUE,
                          auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE,
                          group = "g",
                          target = "jags")

... it does not seem to consider the equality constraints at all, even though the output states that:

Constraints:
                                                                     |Slack|
    L51 - (5-L11-L21-L31-L41)                    0.000
    L52 - (5-L12-L22-L32-L42)                    0.000
    0 - (I11+I21+I31+I41+I51)                    0.000
    0 - (I12+I22+I32+I42+I52)                    0.000

I suspect that it is simply because there is overlap between the equality constraints and the default priors? A working model in JAGS would include something like this to achieve effects coding:

 #Piors, item intercepts
  for(k in 1:K){
alpha[1,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[2,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[3,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[4,k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
alpha[5,k] ~ dsum(-alpha[1,k],-alpha[2,k],-alpha[3,k],-alpha[4,k])
  }

  #Priors, item loadings
  for(k in 1:K){
lambda[1,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[2,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[3,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[4,k] ~ dnorm(1,0.01)
lambda[5,k] ~ dsum(5,-lambda[1,k],-lambda[2,k],-lambda[3,k],-lambda[4,k])
  }

My questions is if this is possible to achieve using the blavaan syntax? I am aware that I can assign individual priors to each parameter, but "dsum" does not seem to affect the jags model output file at all. I have tried different options, but no luck so far.

Any help is much appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: blavaan syntax with equality constraints
messages.body_plain:
Sixten,

Thanks for the report; that constraint specification should have worked. I believe that something changed in lavaan, which caused blavaan to ignore the constraints. It should now be fixed on github, and I will try to get a new version to CRAN soon:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan

One thing about your constraints: instead of

0 == I11 + I12 + ...

blavaan will want you to put one variable on the lhs:

I11 == -I12 - I13 - ...

The reason is that, in doing the translation to jags, we always need one variable to be a function of others, and blavaan currently isn't smart enough to do that on its own.

Ed

Sixten

Adding to this, you can use the measEq.syntax() function from semTools to build the syntax for this types of models with differents types of constraints. And in this case it already defines the first indicator parameter in function of the others, avoiding the issue that Ed mentioned

Here is an example with the HolzingerSwineford1939 data set

                       ID.fac = "FX",
                       data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
                       group = "school")
cat(as.character(mtest))

f_test <- bcfa(as.character(mtest),
               data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
               group = "school",
               target = "jags",
               adapt=4000, burnin=15000,sample=5000)
summary(f_test)

On Mon, 2020-09-21 at 02:24 -0700, Robin Tschötschel wrote:
> I have one dummy-coded exogenous variable (an experimental condition indicator) in a path analysis. Maybe this is a stupid question, but do I need to indicate this in my model specification (for example by giving it thresholds)?

I believe that an exogenous variable coded as 0/1 should "just work" without needing to do anything extra.

>
> And maybe one last: blavaan doesn't support non-normally distributed indicator variables, right? the only way to work with non-normal data being transformations applied prior to estimation?

Correct, non-normal variables are not there yet. We hope to implement functionality for ordinal variables in the future. The only option for now is to export the model syntax (using mcmcfile=TRUE), then edit the jags or stan file yourself. But that would probably not be trivial.

Ed

Alternatively, it might be possible to modify what you send to discFun in order to skip over errors. I haven't tried it to know whether it will work, but possibly

pred = function(fit){
res <- try(lavPredict(fit, type="ov"))
if(inherits(res, 'try-error')) res <- NA
res
}

Ed
